correctness.rationale: A common open hemisphere exists throughout the stated parameter range; two tangent geodesics delimit the hull. The spherical cosine and sine laws determine tangent angles u and v, and Girard plus spherical sector area gives the exact area. Differentiation yields the strictly positive derivative 2 sin(r)(cos(r)-cos(t))/(sin(t)sqrt(sin(t)^2-sin(r)^2)). Expansions at the two endpoints give the proved 3/2 and 1/2 laws and invert to the claimed 2/3 and quadratic radius laws. The actual standalone Python program numerically passed 27 comparisons, independently triangulating spherical polygon hulls. The analytic argument, not its finite tests, proves the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Finite-level radius of a spherical illumination body is the natural quantitative completion of the recently introduced model. The exact all-level profile makes numerical inversion unnecessary and reveals a curvature-sensitive square-root area cusp and sharp quadratic terminal radius law at an antipodal-contact boundary. This is not merely a perturbative restatement of the general small-level theorem, a numerical lookup or an arbitrary finite slice; the object and both endpoints are intrinsic.
